s.en: Create and run a new container from an image
s.es: crea un contenedor nuevo y ejecuta un comando en él

p.es: Imagen de la que se crea el contenedor (nginx, ubuntu:22.04, usuario/app:1.0).
p.en: Image to create the container from (nginx, ubuntu:22.04, user/app:1.0).

p.es: Comando (y argumentos) a ejecutar dentro, en vez del que trae la imagen.
p.en: Command (and arguments) to run inside, instead of the image's default.

tip.es: «-p 8080:80» = PUERTO_DEL_ANFITRIÓN:PUERTO_DEL_CONTENEDOR. Montar «/var/run/docker.sock» o «/» dentro de un contenedor equivale a darle control del anfitrión.
tip.en: "-p 8080:80" = HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT. Mounting "/var/run/docker.sock" or "/" inside a container is equivalent to giving it control of the host.

o.es: Segundo plano: no ocupa tu terminal.
o.en: Detached: does not occupy your terminal.

o.es: Mantiene la entrada estándar abierta.
o.en: Keep STDIN open.

o.es: Asigna una terminal.
o.en: Allocate a pseudo-TTY.

o.es: Borra el contenedor automáticamente al terminar.
o.en: Automatically remove the container when it exits.

o.es: Nombre del contenedor.
o.en: Assign a name to the container.

o.es: Publica un puerto: -p 8080:80 abre el 8080 de tu equipo hacia el 80 del contenedor.
o.en: Publish a port: -p 8080:80 opens port 8080 on your host to port 80 in the container.

o.es: Publica todos los puertos expuestos en puertos aleatorios.
o.en: Publish all exposed ports to random ports.

o.es: Monta una ruta o volumen del anfitrión en el contenedor (:ro = solo lectura).
o.en: Mount a host path or volume in the container (:ro = read-only).

o.es: Montaje detallado (type=bind,source=…,target=…).
o.en: Detailed mount (type=bind,source=…,target=…).

o.es: Define una variable de entorno.
o.en: Set an environment variable.

o.es: Lee variables de un archivo.
o.en: Read in a file of environment variables.

o.es: Directorio de trabajo dentro del contenedor.
o.en: Working directory inside the container.

o.es: Usuario con el que se ejecuta dentro (por defecto root).
o.en: User to run as inside (default root).

o.es: Red a la que se conecta (bridge, host, none o una propia).
o.en: Network to connect to (bridge, host, none or a custom one).

o.es: Política de reinicio: no, on-failure, always, unless-stopped.
o.en: Restart policy: no, on-failure, always, unless-stopped.

o.es: Da al contenedor casi todos los permisos del anfitrión (¡peligroso!).
o.en: Gives the container nearly all host privileges (dangerous!).

o.es: Añade una capacidad de Linux (p. ej. NET_ADMIN).
o.en: Add a Linux capability (e.g. NET_ADMIN).

o.es: Quita una capacidad.
o.en: Drop a Linux capability.

o.es: Espacio de procesos (--pid=host comparte los del anfitrión: peligroso).
o.en: PID namespace (--pid=host shares the host's: dangerous).

o.es: Da acceso a un dispositivo del anfitrión.
o.en: Add a host device to the container.

o.es: Límite de memoria (512m, 2g).
o.en: Memory limit (512m, 2g).

o.es: Límite de CPU (1.5).
o.en: Number of CPUs.

o.es: Sistema de archivos raíz de solo lectura.
o.en: Mount the container's root filesystem as read only.

o.es: Opciones de seguridad (seccomp, apparmor, no-new-privileges).
o.en: Security options (seccomp, apparmor, no-new-privileges).

o.es: Cambia el programa de entrada de la imagen.
o.en: Overwrite the default ENTRYPOINT of the image.

o.es: Nombre de host dentro del contenedor.
o.en: Container host name.

o.es: Servidor DNS.
o.en: Set custom DNS servers.

o.es: Añade una entrada a /etc/hosts del contenedor.
o.en: Add a custom host-to-IP mapping.

o.es: Etiqueta del contenedor.
o.en: Set meta data on a container.

o.es: Plataforma (linux/amd64, linux/arm64).
o.en: Set platform if server is multi-platform capable.

o.es: Cuándo descargar la imagen (always, missing, never).
o.en: Pull image before running.

o.es: Ejecuta un proceso init como PID 1.
o.en: Run an init inside the container.

o.es: Tamaño de /dev/shm.
o.en: Size of /dev/shm.

o.es: Monta un tmpfs (memoria).
o.en: Mount a tmpfs directory.

o.es: Límite de recursos.
o.en: Ulimit options.

o.es: Espacio de nombres de usuario.
o.en: User namespace to use.
Attach to STDIN, STDOUT or STDERR.
Add an annotation to the container (passed through to the OCI runtime).
Block IO weight (relative weight) accepts a weight value between 10 and 1000.
Block IO weight (relative device weight, format: DEVICE_NAME:WEIGHT).
CPU shares (relative weight)

Set the cgroup namespace mode for the container. host: run the container in the host's cgroup namespace private: run the container in its own private cgroup namespace "": (unset) use the daemon's default configuration (host on cgroup v1, private on cgroup v2)

Path to cgroups under which the cgroup for the container will be created. If the path is not absolute, the path is considered to be relative to the cgroups path of the init process. Cgroups will be created if they do not already exist.
Write the container ID to the file
Limit the number of CPUs available for execution by the container.
Limit the percentage of CPU available for execution by a container running on a Windows daemon.
Limit the CPU CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) period
CPUs in which to allow execution (0-3, 0,1)
Memory nodes (MEMs) in which to allow execution (0-3, 0,1). Only effective on NUMA systems.
Limit the CPU CFS (Completely Fair Scheduler) quota
Limit the CPU real-time period in microseconds
Limit the CPU real-time runtime in microseconds
Override the key sequence for detaching a container; key is a single character from the [a-Z] range, or ctrl-value, where value is one of: a-z, @, ^, [, ,, or _.

Add a rule to the cgroup allowed devices list. The rule is expected to be in the format specified in the Linux kernel documentation (Documentation/cgroup-v1/devices.txt): - type: a (all), c (char), or b (block); - major and minor: either a number, or * for all; - mode: a composition of r (read), w (write), and m (mknod(2)).
Limit read rate from a device (e.g. --device-read-bps=/dev/sda:1mb)
Limit read rate from a device (e.g. --device-read-iops=/dev/sda:1000)
Limit write rate to a device (e.g. --device-write-bps=/dev/sda:1mb)
Limit write rate to a device (e.g. --device-write-iops=/dev/sda:1000)
Set custom DNS search domains (Use --dns-search=. if you don't wish to set the search domain)
Set custom DNS options
Container NIS domain name

Expose a port, or a range of ports (e.g. --expose=3300-3310) informs Docker that the container listens on the specified network ports at runtime. Docker uses this information to interconnect containers using links and to set up port redirection on the host system.
Add additional groups to run as
Print usage statement
Sets the container's interface IPv4 address (e.g., 172.23.0.9)
Sets the container's interface IPv6 address (e.g., 2001:db8::1b99)
Sets the IPC mode for the container. The following values are accepted:
Isolation specifies the type of isolation technology used by containers. Note that the default on Windows server is process, and the default on Windows client is hyperv. Linux only supports default.
Kernel memory limit; S is an optional suffix which can be one of b, k, m, or g.
Read in a line delimited file of labels
Add link to another container.
Add one or more link-local IPv4/IPv6 addresses to the container's interface
Logging driver for the container. Default is defined by daemon --log-driver flag. Warning: the docker logs command works only for the json-file and journald logging drivers.
Logging driver specific options.
Memory soft limit; S is an optional suffix which can be one of b, k, m, or g.
Combined memory plus swap limit; S is an optional suffix which can be one of b, k, m, or g.
Container MAC address (e.g., 92:d0:c6:0a:29:33)
Add network-scoped alias for the container
Whether to disable OOM Killer for the container or not.
Tune the host's OOM preferences for containers (accepts -1000 to 1000)
Tune the container's pids (process IDs) limit. Set to -1 to have unlimited pids for the container.

Set the UTS mode for the container. The only possible type is host, meaning to use the host's UTS namespace inside the container. Note: the host mode gives the container access to changing the host's hostname and is therefore considered insecure.
Storage driver options per container
Signal to stop the container.
Timeout (in seconds) to stop a container, or -1 to disable timeout.
Configure namespaced kernel parameters at runtime
Proxy received signals to the process (non-TTY mode only). SIGCHLD, SIGSTOP, and SIGKILL are not proxied. The default is true.
Tune a container's memory swappiness behavior. Accepts an integer between 0 and 100.
Container's volume driver. This driver creates volumes specified either from a Dockerfile's VOLUME instruction or from the docker run -v flag. See docker-volume-create(1) for full details.
Mount volumes from the specified container(s)
